pr_title: streamingest,sql: better tenant status for replicated tenants
pr_body:
Currently the status of the destination tenant during replication is `ADD` which is not ideal.

This commit changes the status to be, roughly, the status of the replication job. The destination tenant status can be:
`DROP` - the tenant was dropped.
`ADD` - the job is still pending, not replicating yet (should be transient).
`REPLICATING` - the replication job is running (perhaps pause was requested).
`REPLICATION PAUSED` - the replication job was paused.
`ACTIVE` - there was a cutover and now the tenant is active.

These are all OK statuses, if we get any other job status:
`failed`, `reverting`, `succeeded`, `canceled`, `cancel-requested`, `revert-failed`.
(this should be an exhaustive list) then we consider the status unexpected and in that case the `SHOW TENANT` command will print:
`REPLICATION UNKNOWN (%s)`
for example:
`REPLICATION UNKNOWN (succeeded)`

Epic: CRDB-18752
Fixes: #93446

Release note: None

Thanks for getting this out! One question that we discussed offline, is whether it's worth keeping those builtins until we have a home for all the information in the  `StreamIngestionStats` proto. Sometimes it is useful during escalations and live debugging to have some of these internal tools that just dump everything in JSON instead of having to string together the information from different places in the database. I could see the JSON builtin in particular being part of our "observability for developers" toolkit. Curious what y'all think?

good question - can't we get all of that from the jobs table?

FTR this PR will have a circular dependency if we keep the builtins :( the jobs package is using builtins and with my change here builtins will use the jobs package. currently we avoid the cycle because of the ccl hook (builtins call the hook, not jobs directly).

> good question - can't we get all of that from the jobs table?

I think we can get most of the fields except `ReplicationLagInfo` which contains computed durations/metrics. Another new reason to keep the builtins is https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C03JCUUSCD6/p1671013162310789 although making it a noop might break the dependency cycle that you were running into. 

Another alternative would be to keep the GetStreamIngestionStats method as it is i.e takes in a txn and loads the job, and pull out the guts of the processing after we have the job details into an exported method. Then the builtin can continue existing, and we can call `ConstructStreamIngestionStats` or whatever we decide to call the method that constructs the stats given a details/progress.

issue_context.title: c2c: `SHOW TENANT` status can be made more informative when replication is ongoing
issue_context.body:
Currently, `SHOW TENANT` shows 3 statuses. `ACTIVE`, `ADD`, `DROP`. If a tenant has an associated replication job it would be useful from an observability point of view to have a:
-  `REPLICATION RUNNING` or `REPLICATING` if a replication job is running
-  `REPLICATION PAUSED` if a replication job is paused (either by user or on error)

Epic: CRDB-18752

Jira issue: CRDB-22336

review_comments: Overall I like this approach, but I wonder if we are providing too much of a window into our internal job state to users. PauseRequested and Pending are transient states that the job goes through in our state machine. Do we think we want to explain to the end user what these states really mean?

WDYT about mapping:
StatusPauseRequested to REPLICATING because if pause was only requested then we are still replicating.
StatusPending to ADD because we just started the replication.

done, hopefully this makes sense.
btw I'll add datadriven tests for those states the minute you merge you pr!
I like this! and yes getting that PR in is first on my list, it keeps running into issues
